assignmentTitle: Comparison of Spur and Helical Gears in Industrial Power Transmission
courseOutcome: CO1: Apply principle of Spur & Helical gear design for industrial application.

criteria.title: Engineering Problem Charter & Technical Scope
criteria.description: Student confirms engineering scope, operating criteria, comparison objectives, syllabus boundary, and acknowledgment of zero numerical helical force calculations.

criteria.title: Parallel Gear Assembly Visualisation & Component Callout Mapping
criteria.description: Deterministic identification of 10 assembly callouts across parallel spur and helical gear drives (1: Spur Input Shaft, 2: Driving Spur Pinion, 3: Driven Spur Gear, 4: Spur Output Shaft, 5: Support Bearing — Spur, 6: Helical Input Shaft, 7: Driving Helical Pinion, 8: Driven Helical Gear, 9: Helical Output Shaft, 10: Support Bearing — Helical).

criteria.title: Gear-Type Identification & Geometric Architecture
criteria.description: Accurate identification of tooth orientation relative to shaft axis, normal and transverse module relations (mt = mn / cos beta), pressure angle transformation (tan alpha_t = tan alpha_n / cos beta), and virtual teeth (z' = z / cos^3 beta).

criteria.title: Tooth Engagement Kinematics & Contact Line Mechanics
criteria.description: Accurate comparison of sudden full face-width line contact and dynamic impact in spur gears versus gradual, progressive diagonal contact line progression and smoother load transfer in helical gears.

criteria.title: Force Characteristics & 3D Force Vector Resolution
criteria.description: Vectorial and directional analysis of 2D spur forces (Ft, Fr, Fa = 0) versus 3D helical spatial forces (Ft, Fr, Fa), conceptual origin of axial thrust (Fa = Ft * tan beta), and dependence on helix hand and rotation direction.

criteria.title: Bearing Consequences & Shaft Mounting Integration
criteria.description: Accurate determination of bearing arrangements: standard radial deep-groove ball or cylindrical roller bearings for spur drives versus thrust-capable paired tapered roller or angular contact bearings for helical drives with rigid housing retention.

criteria.title: Dynamic Transmission Behaviour, Noise & Velocity Limits
criteria.description: Comparison of contact ratio (transverse ratio vs total overlap ratio), pitch-line velocity operating regimes, Barth velocity factor (Cv) dynamics, and acoustic whine suppression in enclosed drives.

criteria.title: Manufacturing Processes, Capital Cost & Maintenance
criteria.description: Analysis of tooling complexity (straight-axis hobbing vs helix lead synchronization), axial alignment sensitivity, field maintenance simplicity, and capital expenditure justification.

criteria.title: Industrial Application Requirement & Selection Matrix
criteria.description: Deterministic evaluation of six industrial application profiles (cement apron conveyor, EV reduction gearbox, overhead crane winch, centrifugal gas compressor, agricultural seed planter, paper mill drying cylinder) matching gear type and technical justification (6 x 0.25 = 1.5 marks).

criteria.title: Engineering Decision Canvas: Selection & Defense
criteria.description: Faculty evaluation of open-ended engineering decision defending spur vs helical selection for an industrial case (low-speed bucket elevator, high-speed blower, or mining slurry pump) across speed, noise, bearing complexity, casing design, and lifecycle economics.

criteria.title: Professional Reflection & Transmission Design Synthesis
criteria.description: Faculty evaluation of student synthesis summarizing fundamental transmission differences, formulating a practical 3-point rule-of-thumb decision heuristic for junior designers, and reflecting on initial capital expenditure versus operational reliability and lifecycle cost.
